description: Artificial Intelligence Act (EU 2024/1689) regulating AI systems in the EU, plus the AI Office Decision establishing the enforcement body
applicability: AI system providers, deployers, distributors, importers, and the European AI Office

source_documents.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (AI Act)
Commission Decision of 24 January 2024 establishing the European Artificial Intelligence Office

requirements.requirement_text: Prohibited: AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or group, causing significant harm
requirements.applicable_entity: All AI system providers and deployers

requirements.requirement_text: Prohibited: AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities of persons due to age, disability, or specific social or economic situation, to materially distort behaviour causing significant harm
requirements.applicable_entity: All AI system providers and deployers

requirements.requirement_text: Prohibited: AI systems for social scoring by public authorities, evaluating or classifying natural persons based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, leading to detrimental treatment

Prohibited: AI systems for assessing or predicting the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on profiling or personality traits (except when supporting human assessment based on objective facts)
Prohibited: AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage
requirements.applicable_entity: All AI system providers and deployers

requirements.requirement_text: Prohibited: AI systems that infer emotions in the workplace or educational institutions, except for medical or safety reasons

Prohibited: Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement, except for targeted search for victims, prevention of threats to life, or locating suspects of serious crimes (subject to authorisation)

High-risk AI systems are those: (a) used as safety components of products covered by EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, or (b) falling within use cases listed in Annex III (biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice)
Providers of high-risk AI systems shall establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system throughout the entire lifecycle of the AI system
High-risk AI systems using machine learning shall be developed using training, validation and testing datasets that meet quality criteria: relevant, representative, free of errors, complete

Technical documentation shall be drawn up before the high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service, and kept up to date. Documentation must demonstrate compliance with the requirements of this Chapter
High-risk AI systems shall be designed to automatically record logs (event logging) during operation, to ensure traceability of the AI system's functioning
High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to ensure their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately

High-risk AI systems shall be designed to allow effective human oversight while the AI system is in use, including the ability to correctly interpret the system's output and to intervene or interrupt the system
High-risk AI systems shall be designed to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle

Providers of high-risk AI systems shall: ensure compliance with requirements in Chapter III Section 2, have a quality management system, draw up technical documentation, keep logs, ensure conformity assessment, register in EU database, take corrective actions, cooperate with authorities

Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put in place a quality management system covering: strategy for regulatory compliance, design procedures, development procedures, examination and validation, resource management, document management

Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall: use systems in accordance with instructions, assign human oversight, ensure input data is relevant, monitor operation, keep logs for at least 6 months, inform workers when AI is used, conduct fundamental rights impact assessments (for public bodies)
Prior to deploying a high-risk AI system in Annex III areas, deployers that are public bodies (or private entities providing public services) shall perform a fundamental rights impact assessment

Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to directly interact with natural persons are designed so that the natural person is informed they are interacting with an AI system (unless obvious from circumstances)
Providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format as artificially generated or manipulated
Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems shall inform natural persons exposed to the system of its operation

Providers of general-purpose AI models shall: draw up and keep up-to-date technical documentation, make information available to downstream providers, put in place a policy to comply with copyright law, publish a sufficiently detailed summary of training content

Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall: perform model evaluations, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track and report serious incidents, ensure adequate cybersecurity protection
requirements.applicable_entity: GPAI model providers with systemic risk

requirements.requirement_text: High-risk AI systems shall be registered in the EU database before being placed on the market or put into service. Deployers that are public authorities shall also register their use
requirements.applicable_entity: High-risk AI system providers and public deployers

requirements.requirement_text: High-risk AI systems shall undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market. For Annex III systems, providers may choose self-assessment; for biometric systems, third-party assessment is required

EU AI Office and competent authorities may request access to the training, validation and testing datasets used for high-risk AI systems and GPAI models, including through technical tools and application programming interfaces

Administrative fines up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited AI practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other violations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for incorrect information to authorities
requirements.applicable_entity: All AI system providers and deployers

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall perform the tasks set out in Article 3 for the purposes of implementing and enforcing the AI Act
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall develop tools, methodologies and benchmarks for evaluating capabilities of general-purpose AI models, in particular for GPAI models with systemic risks
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall monitor the implementation and application of rules on general-purpose AI models and systems
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall investigate possible infringements of rules on general-purpose AI models, including collecting complaints and assisting Commission decisions
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall support implementation of rules on prohibited AI practices and high-risk AI systems, facilitating information exchange between national authorities
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: The AI Office shall provide the Secretariat for the AI Board, and administrative support to the advisory forum and scientific panel
requirements.law_title: Commission Decision establishing the European AI Office

requirements.requirement_text: Application dates: Prohibited practices (Art 5) from 2 February 2025; GPAI rules and governance (Chapters V, VII) from 2 August 2025; High-risk AI requirements from 2 August 2026; Article 6(1) requirements for products in Annex I from 2 August 2027
requirements.applicable_entity: All AI system providers and deployers
